title: HackerRank vs TestGorilla for technical screening: 2025 pricing & features
text:
HackerRank vs TestGorilla for technical screening: 2025 pricing & features
Why compare HackerRank and TestGorilla for technical screening in 2025?
Technical screening has become the critical bottleneck in tech hiring, with companies processing thousands of candidates while struggling to identify genuine coding expertise. The difference between platforms that offer deep technical assessment versus general skills testing can mean the success or failure of your engineering hiring program.
HackerRank currently processes around 172,800 technical skill assessment submissions daily, serving over 3,000 customers across industries. This scale reflects a fundamental shift in how companies evaluate technical talent, moving beyond surface-level testing to comprehensive coding assessments that mirror real engineering work.
The depth of technical evaluation matters more than ever. While general testing platforms can screen for basic competencies, engineering teams need assessments that validate actual coding ability, problem-solving approaches, and production-ready skills. The choice between a specialized technical platform and a general assessment tool directly impacts your ability to identify and hire qualified developers.
2025 pricing breakdown: HackerRank vs TestGorilla
Understanding the true cost of technical screening requires looking beyond headline prices to examine what's actually included in each tier and how overage charges can impact your budget.
HackerRank pricing structure
HackerRank offers transparent, tiered pricing starting at
$165 per month
for the Starter plan when billed annually. The Pro tier costs
$375 per month
billed annually, while Enterprise plans feature custom pricing. Both self-serve tiers include Screen and Interview products, advanced plagiarism detection, and access to thousands of coding questions.
Each plan includes a set number of candidate attempts (120 annually for Starter and 300 for Pro) with overages charged at $20 per additional attempt. The Enterprise tier unlocks the
full 7,500-question library
and can handle up to 100,000 candidates simultaneously.
TestGorilla pricing model
TestGorilla operates on a credit-based system, starting at
$142 per month
billed annually. Their model uses a 1:3 credit ratio where one candidate invitation equals one credit, but a full evaluation consumes three credits. This usage-based approach means actual costs can vary significantly based on your evaluation needs.
Their
subscription plans have
a standard 12-month duration, with credits that don't roll over between billing periods. While TestGorilla advertises flexibility, the credit system can make it challenging to predict actual monthly costs, especially for high-volume hiring.
Coding assessment depth and content libraries
The breadth and depth of technical assessment content determines whether you can accurately evaluate candidates across different roles, experience levels, and technology stacks.
HackerRank
supports 55+ programming
languages, enabling comprehensive assessment across virtually any technical stack your team uses. This extensive language support means you can evaluate frontend developers in JavaScript, backend engineers in Python or Java, mobile developers in Swift or Kotlin, and systems programmers in C++ or Rust, all within the same platform.
TestGorilla publicly lists only
12 coding tests
across 20 languages, limiting your ability to assess specialized roles or emerging technologies. While they offer additional non-technical tests, their coding assessment library lacks the depth needed for thorough technical evaluation. According to recent data,
81% of employers
now use skills-based hiring, making comprehensive language coverage essential.
Real-world project support
HackerRank includes
multi-file project questions
that simulate actual development environments. Candidates work with realistic codebases, implement features across multiple files, and demonstrate their ability to navigate complex project structures. These skills directly translate to on-the-job performance.
TestGorilla's coding tests focus primarily on algorithmic challenges and single-file exercises. Their
skill library uses
randomization to minimize guessing but lacks the depth of real-world project simulation that engineering teams need to evaluate practical coding ability.
Proctoring, AI & cheating prevention
Maintaining assessment integrity has become critical as AI tools and cheating methods grow more sophisticated. The difference in proctoring capabilities can determine whether your assessments accurately reflect candidate abilities.
HackerRank's integrity stack has proven its effectiveness against AI cheating tools. As the platform notes, "Our AI plagiarism detection successfully flagged the candidate for plagiarism in all three questions." The Proctor Mode captures session replays, providing clear evidence of any external tool usage. The platform combines multiple detection layers including advanced plagiarism detection, leaked question protection, and behavioral analysis.
TestGorilla offers basic proctoring features but lacks the comprehensive integrity measures needed for technical assessments. AI-powered proctoring can
reduce costs by
70-80% compared to live proctoring, making it essential for high-volume screening. However, without robust detection capabilities, these savings mean little if candidates can easily circumvent the system.
Recent industry data shows that
implementing AI-based proctoring
and device monitoring effectively prevents cheating and ensures secure online assessments. This makes platform choice crucial for maintaining hiring standards.
AI Interviewer & automated insights
HackerRank's AI Interviewer
closely simulates real
interview experiences, adapting to candidate skill levels and asking follow-up questions to understand their thinking process. The system provides hints without revealing answers, creating a more authentic evaluation experience that reduces interview anxiety while maintaining assessment rigor.
TestGorilla has introduced
AI-powered scoring for
essay questions but lacks the sophisticated AI interviewing capabilities that technical roles require. Their system focuses on general assessment automation rather than the specific needs of technical evaluation, leaving gaps in the candidate experience and assessment quality.
Customer results & market sentiment
Enterprise success metrics
Red Hat achieved remarkable efficiency gains with HackerRank,
reducing live technical
interviews by over 60%. This dramatic reduction came from the platform disqualifying 63% of phase one candidates, allowing engineering teams to focus only on qualified prospects. The time-to-fill improvement meant Red Hat could secure top talent faster in competitive markets.
External reviews consistently favor HackerRank's technical screening capabilities, with users scoring it
92 for likeliness
to recommend and 90 for plan renewal intentions. The platform maintains a Net Emotional Footprint of +96, with 97% positive user sentiment.
As noted by Ashish Peshave, Global Talent Acquisition Partner at ZS: "The most valuable feature of HackerRank is its simplicity and user-friendly interface. As a Talent Acquisition Manager, I can easily create technical assessments, which is a huge advantage. Hiring managers often don't have the time to manually review candidates' technical capabilities, but with HackerRank, I can leverage its platform (using AI if needed) to identify the right skills, create assessments, and quickly review them with hiring managers for any necessary edits."
Which platform fits your tech hiring roadmap?
Selecting between HackerRank and TestGorilla depends on your organization's technical hiring maturity, volume, and growth trajectory.
Enterprise and high-volume scenarios
For companies hiring at scale, HackerRank's ability to
test up to
100,000 candidates simultaneously provides unmatched capacity. More than
25% of Fortune
100 companies rely on the platform, validating its enterprise readiness. The platform's 40+ ATS integrations, including Workday and Oracle, ensure seamless workflow integration.
Growing technical teams
Organizations building their technical assessment capabilities benefit from HackerRank's structured approach. The platform grows with your needs, from basic screening with the Starter plan to comprehensive evaluation with Enterprise features. Industry data shows that
82% of companies
use pre-employment assessments as reliable indicators of skills, making platform scalability essential.
TestGorilla may suit companies with mixed hiring needs beyond technical roles, but its limited coding assessment depth becomes a liability as technical hiring requirements mature. The credit-based pricing model can also create budget uncertainty for growing teams with fluctuating hiring volumes.
Key takeaways
The comparison between HackerRank and TestGorilla reveals fundamental differences in technical assessment philosophy and capabilities. HackerRank's specialized focus on developer evaluation, combined with its comprehensive language support, advanced integrity features, and proven enterprise results, positions it as the clear choice for serious technical hiring.
With
over 2,500 companies
globally using HackerRank and
172,800 daily assessments
processed, the platform has proven its ability to handle technical screening at any scale. The depth of HackerRank's
55+ language support
and 7,500-question library ensures you can evaluate any technical role thoroughly.
For organizations committed to building strong engineering teams, HackerRank's
Screen product
delivers the assessment depth, integrity safeguards, and candidate experience needed to identify and hire top technical talent. The investment in specialized technical screening pays dividends through better hiring decisions, reduced time-to-fill, and stronger engineering teams.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the key difference between HackerRank and TestGorilla for technical screening?
HackerRank focuses on deep technical evaluation with multi-file projects, 55+ language coverage, and advanced integrity controls, while TestGorilla emphasizes general skills testing. For engineering roles, the specialized depth in HackerRank assessments yields stronger signals about real-world coding ability at scale.
How do 2025 prices and overages compare between the two platforms?
In 2025, HackerRank offers Starter at $165/month and Pro at $375/month when billed annually, with overages at $20 per additional attempt; annual Pro also supports $15 pre-purchased attempts. TestGorilla uses a credit-based model that starts around $142/month billed annually, and actual spend varies with how many credits full evaluations consume.
How deep is the coding content and language coverage on each platform?
HackerRank supports 55+ programming languages and provides access to a large coding question library, including multi-file projects for realistic work. TestGorilla publicly lists roughly a dozen coding tests across about 20 languages, which limits coverage for specialized or emerging stacks.
What integrity and AI features does HackerRank offer to prevent cheating?
HackerRank combines AI-powered plagiarism detection, webcam image analysis, Proctor Mode session replays, leaked question protection, and behavioral analysis to deter cheating. These layered controls help ensure results reflect a candidate’s own skills while keeping high-volume screening efficient.
Which platform is better for enterprise or high-volume hiring?
Enterprises and teams hiring at high volume benefit from HackerRank’s scale and ATS integrations, including the ability to test large candidate pools simultaneously. Teams with mixed non-technical hiring may consider TestGorilla, but its limited coding depth can become a constraint as technical hiring matures.
Do HackerRank self-serve plans include live technical interviews?
Yes. Per the HackerRank pricing page on
hackerrank.com
, the self-serve Starter and Pro plans include Screen and Interview, advanced plagiarism detection, and 120 and 300 annual candidate attempts respectively, with $20 per additional attempt. Annual Pro also supports $15 pre-purchased attempts.
